analysis.title: Where Things Stand
key_insights: HF unwind is very real and extended, but broader positioning remains elevated, the Fed has not come to the rescue and the AI earnings debate is unresolved. Investors are frozen, finding it hard to add shorts or buy the dip.
GS prime: fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42.3%, the 1st percentile over the past year. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell more than 22 pts since start of October to 48.2%, a five-year low.
SPX top of book liquidity fell to about $4mm, near YTD lows. Thin liquidity likely contributes to the magnitude of realized vol.

The 6-week straddle discussed the prior weekend realized 2x over a 5-day period, and its price more than doubled from 4% to 8.2%. Convexity trades at panic levels seen in 2025 liberation day, 2020 covid, 2022 and 2010-11 episodes. The desk leans toward calling it an 'AI conviction crisis'.

Commodities last week: copper hit by macro sentiment despite record Chinese tightness, precious metals in orderly deleveraging with CTAs still sellers, oil rallies capped by macro with back end vol rich and put skew cheap.

GS vol panic index hit 9.8 of 10 last Friday. Readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief, but the Fed is hiking, and in five episodes with panic above 9 in a hiking regime the subsequent three-month return averaged just +0.4%.

Positioning is mixed: GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at the 75th percentile, US equity MFs and ETFs took in nearly $170bn since start of Q4, and asset manager equity futures length is at the 82nd percentile over the decade. There is HF capitulation but not a broad washout.

Q4 2018 parallels: the October 2018 panic episode was followed by another 6.8% decline over three months. Versus 2018, equities (especially tech) are close, credit is not, rates have done half the work, FX has outperformed massively, and havens (gold and JPY) went the wrong way.
GIR's Ben Snider lists three bottom conditions: improved confidence in AI earnings trajectory, a dovish Fed signal, and a major decline in investor positioning.

Flows desk view: vol is more clearly panicked than positioning is washed out. VXN closed Friday at its highest since COVID and VXSMH at an all-time high, with the front of the vol curve sharply inverted.
Desk prefers underwriting vol over chasing stocks. Selling puts at levels where one would add length looks attractive, especially in tech where the vol repricing is most extreme.

sector_views.rationale: VXSMH at series all-time high, so implied vol looks overshot, favoring put selling over buying protection or delta.
Vol repricing most extreme in tech, so selling puts at desired entry levels is preferred to buying delta.

earnings_insights: AI earnings debate remains unresolved. Capital intensity, financing requirements, return on investment and valuations are being questioned at the same time.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A hiking Fed differs from past panic episodes and has historically meant weak subsequent returns after panic readings above 9.
Readings above 9.5 have signaled near-term relief, but conditions differ today.

trade_ideas.description: Sell puts in tech and semis at levels where comfortable adding length, underwriting overshot implied vol rather than buying delta
trade_ideas.rationale: Investors get paid considerably more to take equity risk with the ability to add at lower entry levels.
trade_ideas.risk: Still taking downside risk if the selloff becomes sustained.

risk_factors: Further HF deleveraging and thin liquidity amplifying realized vol.
Elevated non-HF positioning could drive another leg lower, as in Q4 2018.
Hiking Fed with no dovish signal.
Unresolved AI earnings and financing debate.
